title: The AI Data Editor: Agents That Rerun 4,452 Economics Papers
summary: A new NBER workflow ran an LLM over 4,452 replication packages and flagged discrepancies in 3,460 articles, while benchmarks show coding agents now reproduce most social-science results when given code and data. We dig into what those flags mean, why agents must never see the answer key, and how Lucas can build a blind, sandboxed reproduction check this week.
shownotes:
NBER w35782 (Schwartz, Andrews, Shapiro): an LLM workflow that reproduces, improves and extends 4,452 published replication packages; 3,460 articles flagged, 496 with 10x+ speedups, 923 extensions
What a discrepancy flag does and does not mean: a lead for a human editor, not a verdict
Three regimes of reproduction: code and data (Alizadeh et al.), methods and data only (Kohler et al.), proof checking (Toda)
The confirmation-bias trap: giving agents the paper PDF or confirmatory prompts hurts accuracy on non-reproducible tasks; information isolation and deterministic diffing as the fix
Human-in-the-loop evidence: Brodeur et al. randomised experiment (94% / 91% / 37%) and its caveats
Where this goes: pre-submission checks, meta-science audits, who referees agent-written extensions, Dutch replication funding
This week's build: a blind, sandboxed mini AI data editor with deterministic diffing and a planted canary bug
